mc.prompt: Which pairing identifies an organ and the gamete associated with it?
mc.cue: A gonad is an organ; a gamete is a cell.
mc.explanation: Testes are gonads, and sperm are the associated gametes.

mc.prompt: A voice becomes deeper during puberty. Which classification fits this change?
mc.cue: Decide whether the observation describes a reproductive organ.
mc.explanation: A deeper voice is a physical change associated with maturation, not a reproductive organ.

writing.prompt: Explain how a gonad, a gamete and a reproductive hormone differ. Connect all three using either the ovary or testis.
writing.model: A gonad is an organ. A gamete is a reproductive cell. A hormone is a chemical signal. For example, a testis contains sites of sperm production and cells that release testosterone.
criteria: Uses a coherent example linking a gonad, its gamete and a hormone.

writing.prompt: Why is the statement “a feature that changes at puberty must be a secondary sex characteristic” incorrect? Use two examples.
writing.model: Reproductive organs also develop further at puberty. A testis is a primary characteristic even when sperm production begins; a deepening voice is a secondary characteristic. Classification depends on the kind of structure or feature, not only its timing.
criteria: Explains why timing alone is insufficient.
Contrasts a primary organ with a secondary feature.

worked.label: Worked example
worked.title: Classifying three observations
worked.scenario: A student lists an ovary, an egg and a rise in estrogen. Are these three examples of the same thing?
steps: Identify the level of organization. The ovary is an organ and a gonad.
Identify the cell. The egg is a gamete produced through processes in the ovary.
Identify the signal. Estrogen is a hormone that can act on target tissues.
Connect them: cells in an ovarian follicle release estrogen while an oocyte develops within the follicle. Related does not mean interchangeable.

guided.label: Practise with support
guided.title: Apply the explanation
guided.instruction: Try both questions. Use the hint to revise your thinking after an incorrect answer.

items.prompt: A testis begins producing sperm at puberty. How should the testis be classified?
items.hint: Ask whether it is a reproductive organ or a cell.
items.explanation: The testis is a reproductive organ. Increased activity at puberty does not turn it into a secondary characteristic.

items.prompt: A target tissue has no functioning receptor for a reproductive hormone. What is the best prediction?
items.answer: Its usual response to that hormone will be reduced or absent
options: Its usual response to that hormone will be reduced or absent
items.hint: Recall what makes a cell a target cell.
items.explanation: The hormone must interact with an appropriate receptor to produce its normal response.

new_optional_model: The uterus is a reproductive organ, the egg is a gamete and progesterone is a hormone. A gonad specifically produces gametes and reproductive hormones. The uterus supports development but is not an ovary or testis and does not produce gametes. The word reproductive therefore describes a wider group of organs than the word gonad.
